title: ser_json_* config must only affect serialization-mode JSON schemas, never validation-mode
answers: Why does model_json_schema() say type number for a datetime when ser_json_temporal='seconds'?
validation JSON schema for timedelta shows number with ser_json_timedelta='float' but model accepts 'PT5M'
Should ser_json_temporal change the input/validation schema?
datetime field schema wrong when serializing to unix seconds
body:
Symptom: a model with `ser_json_temporal='seconds'/'milliseconds'` (or `ser_json_timedelta='float'`) produced a validation schema (`model_json_schema()`, which defaults to validation mode) of `{'type': 'number'}` for date/time/datetime/timedelta, even though `model_validate_json` still accepts ISO 8601 strings.
Root cause: `pydantic/json_schema.py:GenerateJsonSchema._common_temporal_schema` checked the `ser_json_*` setting without looking at `self.mode`.
Fix pattern: only use the numeric branch when `self.mode == 'serialization' and temporal_format != 'iso8601'`. Otherwise return `{'type': 'string', 'format': <date|time|date-time|duration>}`.
Invariant: `ser_json_*` settings describe output only. Validation mode must describe what validators accept. There is no `val_json_temporal`, and `val_temporal_unit` only changes how a *number* is read; ISO strings are still accepted either way. Any new `ser_*` config read inside the schema generator needs a mode check like this one.
Note: for timedelta under `ser_json_timedelta='float'`, this changed released behaviour (validation schema went from number back to string/duration).
Tests: `tests/test_json_schema.py:test_date_types_ser_json_temporal` asserts both modes.
applies: JSON schema generation for date/time/datetime/timedelta, and any ser_json_* config used in GenerateJsonSchema
